title: Keep one private canonical payload for each admission head and replay receipt
evidence: model.rs:618-753 declares the same 20 head fields twice and moves every field through from_parts; model.rs:799-890 repeats that pattern for the receipt. codec.rs:410-433 and :759-777 reconstruct those payloads field by field, and tree.rs validators reconstruct them again for digest checking.

Receipt reconstruction allocates/copies source_head_bytes, target_head_bytes and retained_predecessor_nodes solely to validate or encode an already borrowed receipt. Complete codec and tree bodies, including cfg test fixtures, were reviewed.

Package design.md, design-schema-v7.md and the conversation-history system require canonical V7 encoding, exact replay closure and bounded retained state; they do not require two private representations.
proposal: Store each existing private Parts value inside its opaque public record and derive Clone/Debug/Eq/PartialEq on Parts. Keep public constructors and const accessors; expose a crate-private borrowed parts accessor for codec and validation. Decode builds Parts once and wraps it after existing checks. Remove the parallel field declarations and field-copy conversion functions. Keep digest recomputation and byte-limit checks; do not expose mutable Parts publicly.
required_contract_changes: None: preserve public opacity, exact Debug field presentation if treated as a diagnostic contract, constructor validation, V7 field order/tags/digest bytes, EOF rejection and byte charges. A hand-written Debug adapter, if needed, is deducted from the estimate.

estimated_net_line_range.basis: About 160-185 lines of duplicate field declarations/conversions become borrowed payload access; deduct 15-35 helper/derive/diagnostic-adapter lines and 15-25 focused vector assertions.
estimated_net_line_range.overlap: Counts model/from_parts and codec/tree reconstruction only. SA-003 counts operation-specific provisional/final construction sites, not these lines. No macro expansion or public getter deletion counted.

verification: Audit only; no builds or tests run.

Retain schema round-trip/digest-damage and tree structural tests. Add exact pre-change head/receipt byte vectors including nonempty closure boxes and retained predecessors; compare encoded charge and formatting where contractual. Confirm borrowed validation performs no closure clone.

title: Share authenticated root and child checks across admission tree readers
evidence: index.rs:858-933 and index/tree_edit.rs:262-375 repeat owner/tree/key/height/digest/count root and child predicates. The path-capturing editor also retains PathStep values; point lookup and least-source lookup do not.

authenticate_path has a distinct nonroot minimum-fanout check and maps malformed shapes to NodeFanout. least_leaf uses child(&child_node) comparison. The duplicate routes are similar but not semantically interchangeable.
proposal: Extract small authenticated_root and authenticated_child functions over the existing ReadLedger and explicit expected root/child descriptor. Reuse them in the three loops while keeping selection, empty-root outcome, fanout policy, error mapping and optional path recording at each caller. Do not route point reads through RootPath or allocate editor paths merely to find a leaf.
required_contract_changes: None. Preserve every existing fail-closed boundary and its error classification. Any decision to unify differing fanout acceptance is a separate authority/defect decision, not part of this reduction.

estimated_net_line_range.basis: Roughly 105-135 repeated predicate/read lines replaced by two 40-55-line helpers and compact calls; deduct 10-20 verification cases.
estimated_net_line_range.overlap: Only descent validation, excluding the dual-tree successor assembly in SA-006 and codec shape checks in SA-001.

verification: Audit only; no builds or tests run.

Exercise empty roots, absent nodes, cross-owner/tree links, mismatched key/digest/count/envelope/height, and nonroot fanout through both lookup and edit paths. Keep existing split/height/command-limit tests and check ReadLedger byte counts remain unchanged.

title: Centralize exact metadata charge exchange and successor head finalization
evidence: publication.rs:297-437 and assignment/mutation.rs:247-446 construct provisional/final heads, measure prior/successor head-plus-receipt metadata, apply checked node-charge deltas, and replace the owner's aggregate charge. terminal/mutation.rs already has a narrow exchange_capacity helper.

writer/begin.rs:18-150 repeats the 18-argument head construction twice and re-reads the prior head after shadowing it solely to recover prior charge. writer/consumption.rs and both settlement paths repeat the same provisional/final accounting pattern.

Tests distinguish retained owner limits, aggregate home limits, authority read bytes, revision overflow, receipt deletion/replacement, empty-ready birth, and compact-terminal settlement. These remain caller-visible acceptance boundaries.
proposal: Add private helpers for checked revision/capacity exchange and for finalizing one caller-supplied head payload with exact old/new metadata and explicit node charge delta. Build operation-specific fields once, compute encoded size from the provisional payload, assign the exact charge, then compute/validate the final digest. Callers retain authority reads, lifecycle selection, receipt construction and operation-specific command-byte preflight. Save prior_charge before constructing the new writer head instead of issuing a second read. Use explicit no-receipt/receipt inputs, not a general deferred-effects engine.
required_contract_changes: None. Preserve arithmetic order where overflow/refusal classification is observable, production and injected limits, all read/write/delete charges, same command atomicity, terminal cleanup residue, exact replay and callback provenance. Do not treat a digest as sufficient old/new equality.

estimated_net_line_range.basis: Remove repeated provisional/final constructor arguments, metadata exchange arithmetic and capacity increments from seven sites; deduct roughly 90-125 helper/caller-adapter lines and 25-40 focused verification lines. Savings exclude generic Parts conversion removed by SA-001.
estimated_net_line_range.overlap: SA-001 owns model/codec/tree field-copy bridges; SA-006 owns node-plan aggregation. Home-store HS-002 proof-command sealing is unrelated and not counted.

verification: Audit only; no builds or tests run.

Retain publication capacity/revision/receipt tests, assignment authority-byte and exhaustion tests, writer replay/settlement/cancellation tests and terminal charge mismatch/final transfer tests. Compare exact head/receipt/capacity bytes and charged totals before/after each lifecycle and fault cut; ensure the removed repeated writer read cannot change required read accounting.

title: Make readiness attempt custody mandatory and consume it once
evidence: attempt.rs:30-36 wraps command, consumer, page, publication and reservation in Option. The constructor always initializes all five; only command needs extraction through &mut self.

Both consume methods take self by value, repeat command-not-taken rejection and receipt consumption, then take the mandatory fields through impossible None errors. The attempt type has no Drop implementation that requires Option extraction.
proposal: Keep command as Option for take_command; store consumer/page/publication/reservation directly. Implement one consuming private receipt-acceptance method that destructures self, checks command absence, consumes the exact receipt and returns mandatory custody. Standalone consume returns the page and drops the reservation/publication; submission moves them into its flight.
required_contract_changes: None. Preserve one-shot ownership, receipt/consumer correlation, home and generation checks, the command-taken precondition, and reservation rollback on every error or standalone consume/drop. Do not make proof or reservation Clone.

estimated_net_line_range.basis: Remove duplicate receipt acceptance and fallible mandatory-field take helpers; deduct the common consuming helper and drop-path verification.
estimated_net_line_range.overlap: Does not simplify the home-store seal/consumer internals in HS-002 or remove independent expected/observed proof correlations.

verification: Audit only; no builds or tests run.

Keep take_command-twice, substituted receipt/consumer, stale reopen, prepared/ready drop capacity, invalidated reservation and reconciliation retry tests. Explicitly check standalone consume and each rejected receipt release the reservation exactly once.

title: Use one internal seal terminal transition for cancel, fail and supersede
evidence: marker_seal.rs:381-427 has three prepared wrappers with identical expected/next custody. Their DomainMutation implementations at :1435-1538 are identical except wrapper type.

Fail and supersede already use prepare_terminal_transition at :809; cancel maintains a separate copy of the same terminal record preparation. AdvanceMutation has different replay behavior and is excluded.
proposal: Introduce one private prepared terminal-transition payload and one TerminalMutation. Keep the public named cancellation/failure/supersede wrappers and methods as small wrappers around that payload. Reuse prepare_terminal_transition for cancellation, with a closed terminal request enum or existing validated lifecycle construction limiting outcomes to Cancelled, Failed(reason), and Superseded.
required_contract_changes: None. Preserve natural identity collision checks, expected-versus-next equality, terminal replay as empty contribution, one-record reconciliation reservation, captured-root custody and refusal to transition a sealed record through an unrelated terminal path.

estimated_net_line_range.basis: Remove two approximately 35-line mutation implementations plus duplicated cancellation preparation and expected/next storage; deduct private payload, wrappers and terminal-path regression overhead.
estimated_net_line_range.overlap: Counts terminal wrappers/implementations only; SA-008 counts error formatting. Advance/seal cursor traversal is not merged.

verification: Audit only; no builds or tests run.

Retain cancel/fail/supersede, natural identity collision, corruption, reopen and exact replay tests. Verify the three typed entry points cannot construct an Open or Sealed terminal mutation and still reserve exactly one record.

title: Finalize the two authenticated index edits through one bounded assembler
evidence: index.rs:428-475 and :749-804 each combine source/target path keys, authenticate reclaimable replay nodes and fresh puts, sum write/delete bytes, concatenate predecessors and construct the same successor footprint.
Ingestion adds one association; assignment adds zero. The custom command-limit check belongs to the ingestion testable path; both enforce the production maximum.
proposal: Create one private finish_index_successor receiving the already authenticated source/target edit results, ReadLedger, prior replay descriptors, explicit association delta and command limit. It performs bounded protection/reclaim/put validation and produces the successor. Keep source/target editing and assigned-label continuity logic at their existing callers.
required_contract_changes: None. Preserve deterministic source-before-target output order, authenticated fresh node IDs, protected predecessor exclusion, retained replay closure, byte accounting and both injected/production limits.

estimated_net_line_range.basis: Two approximately 50-line finish blocks become a roughly 50-60-line helper plus calls; deduct small delta/limit verification additions.
estimated_net_line_range.overlap: Disjoint from descent predicates SA-002 and head/capacity accounting SA-003.

verification: Audit only; no builds or tests run.
Retain first insert, fanout split/propagation, target duplicate and footprint tests; compare exact puts/deletions/predecessor order and charge delta for ingestion versus assignment.

Canonical manual_candidate_entry/manual_cut_entry/manual_accepted_entry and their correlation routines deliberately provide independent byte-layout oracles and must remain independent of production codecs. Readiness fixture marker insertion and writer-admitted insertion are different entry paths.

Have writer ready_proof use a page/assignment quantum count of max(1, association_count) with an explicit final-ready assertion; reuse that helper for ordinary assignment setup with disposition as an argument. required_contract_changes: None. Preserve every scenario, named assertion, feature gate, fault injection point, exact command seed/ordinal, independent canonical byte oracle and distinct admitted versus fixture seed path. Do not make tests use production accounting helpers to compute expected charges.

estimated_net_line_range.overlap: Only the listed test/support files. Excludes durable_builder/support.rs (context only), root-wide tempfile candidates, accepted-proof namespace correction SA-011 and independent canonical encoders.

Run each affected existing test target under its original feature configuration after future implementation. Confirm all fault injections/assertions remain at the same point and both empty and multi-association readiness exercise production APIs.

Compare every Display message and source presence/absence, including readiness wrapped errors remaining unsourced. Retain callback refusal tests and seal read conversion.

title: Retain the durable authenticated tree rather than replacing it with im::OrdMap
evidence: The complete tree/index/codecs implement storage-key ownership, cryptographic child authentication, deterministic operation-scoped node identity, bounded path-copy mutation, exact retained predecessor closure and explicit read/write/delete charges.

The exact im 15.1.0 OrdMap API supplies ordered in-memory operations (get/get_min/update/remove/diff) and structural sharing. Its public API exposes no Beryl storage-node reader, authenticated descriptor, deterministic persisted-node codec or reconciliation reservation boundary.
The current upstream repository is archived; this reinforces the maintenance screen but is not the reason it fails the storage contract.
proposal: Retain the existing bounded durable tree and perform the local predicate/assembly reductions in SA-002 and SA-006. Do not claim the 1,500-plus-line tree/index implementation disappears by collecting records into an immutable map. A collection-backed replacement would retain authentication and replay machinery or materialize the complete operation state, producing no demonstrated net reduction under current authority.
required_contract_changes: Adoption would require an explicit persistent-format/storage architecture redesign and a new proof of bounded memory, command bytes, restart/custody and exact replay. No such change is recommended here.
verification: Audit only; no build, benchmark or advisory scan performed. Screening stopped at architectural incompatibility; no claim of production suitability.

dependency_candidates.evidence: Inspected 2026-09-06. OrdMap is an immutable in-memory B-tree with ordered get/minimum/update/removal/diff. Registry-package manifest declares Rust 1.46.0, MPL-2.0+, edition 2018; normal dependencies include bitmaps, rand_core, rand_xoshiro, sized-chunks and typenum; optional serde/rayon/refpool/testing features. No target-specific dependency section found in that manifest; Windows/MSRV runtime not tested. Upstream describes im as thread-safe and im-rc as the non-thread-safe variant. Upstream GitHub reports archive on 2026-05-03, 486 commits and roughly 1.6k stars; Cargo's official manifest uses sibling im-rc 15.1.0 (related-family adoption, not proof of Beryl storage suitability). No advisory-free claim; comprehensive advisory/dependency review was unnecessary once architecture fit failed. Runtime adapters would still need all durable node I/O/authentication/byte accounting or whole-operation loading, so net saving is unproven and estimated as zero.

title: Retain independent preflight and snapshot proof observations and canonical marker commitments
evidence: Proof preparation and in-command source observation both resolve candidate/cut/accepted ownership. They operate at distinct authority times with different read/error types; an earlier observation cannot establish later validity.

Canonical readiness evidence records every source occurrence in its canonical order, while target custody separately binds private target identity. Source-proof tests retain fixed 434/450-byte candidate/cut entries and accepted proof tests retain 194-byte entries and exact multiplicity limits.

Marker commitment functions combine authenticated summaries and maximum labels with explicit empty/count/overflow checks; replacing them with a generic tree hash would alter canonical semantics. Writer/terminal types carry live generation and exact closure conditions that cannot be dropped because main bootstrap is incomplete.
proposal: Keep both independent read phases and exact proof/terminal custody. Small common pure record predicates may be extracted during adjacent work only if they remain materially smaller after adapters; no positive saving is claimed now. Preserve independent canonical test encoders and the existing SHA-256 domain-separated functions.
required_contract_changes: None for retention. Eliminating execution-time reads, target/occurrence identity, generation fences, exact closure equality or distinct digest semantics would contradict current authority.
verification: Audit only; no builds/tests run. Keep stale-source/asset revision, wrong witness/store, consumer substitution, canonical multiplicity/order, retirement and compact-terminal charge tests.

title: Repair the accepted-proof test's duplicate support module name before using it as validation
evidence: draft_marker_readiness_accepted_proof.rs:32-35 declares both #[path = "draft_marker_readiness_accepted_proof/support.rs"] mod support and #[path = "support/mod.rs"] mod support in the same module.

The fixture support uses crate::support::commit/timestamp for common test helpers, so simply deleting the common declaration would lose those references. This is a static source finding, not a build result.
proposal: Rename the fixture-specific declaration to accepted_support (keep its existing #[path]) and import accepted_support::*; keep common support as support so its qualified commit/timestamp references continue to resolve. Then compile/run this test target under test-faults before relying on it for the simplifications.
required_contract_changes: None. This is test wiring, not product behavior or a new implementation phase.
verification: No build/test run during audit. Future correction: cargo check/test the existing accepted-proof target with test-faults and verify fixed-vector, occurrence count, stale cross-domain evidence and substitution scenarios remain present.
